# Airside by LLM Gateway

> Airside is the self-serve carrier console for LLM providers on LLM Gateway. Providers claim their carrier by verifying an email on their API endpoint's domain, register their model fleet, file fares (pricing) for review, watch their routed traffic, and tune the discount and gateway margin that feed the smart routing election.

## How it works

- Claim your carrier: sign up with a company email whose registrable domain matches your API endpoint's domain (or your published website). Free and disposable email domains are rejected. Claims are reviewed and approved by the LLM Gateway team before going live, and only one live claim exists per provider.
- Register a new provider: a provider that isn't in the catalogue yet can be registered as a custom carrier by submitting its OpenAI-compatible API base URL on the same verified domain.
- Register your fleet: list models with context size, max output, capabilities (streaming, vision, audio, tools, JSON output, reasoning efforts) and per-model rate limits. Non-pricing attributes are editable in place; new listings are reviewed before they enter service.
- File your fares: pricing never changes silently — every price change is a tariff filing that takes effect only after approval. Input, output, cached-input and per-request prices are all supported. One filing can be pending per model at a time.
- Win traffic: routing scores carriers on price (after your discount and the gateway margin you accept), availability, throughput and latency. Lower scores win the request.
- Watch your traffic: requests, errors, tokens, billed traffic and an estimated payout, aggregated per model and per day across every gateway tenant. Aggregates never expose tenant identities, and prompts and responses are never shown to carriers.

## Economics

- Claiming is free where no listing fee is configured; where one is, it is a one-time, non-refundable fee per provider company, charged via Stripe before a claim is approved.
- There is no recurring platform fee and no minimum volume. You share margin only on traffic you actually win.
- You set the gateway margin you accept and an optional routing discount; both take effect immediately and change how your models are scored.
- Estimated payout = billed traffic x (1 - your margin). It is an estimate, not an invoice; actual settlement is governed by a separate written agreement.
- Machine-readable summary: https://airside.llmgateway.io/pricing.md

## The airport metaphor

- Passengers = developers
- Carriers = model providers
- Passports = coding agents
- Visas = reset limits
- Fares = model prices
- Landing fee = the gateway margin
- Dispatch = the routing election
